status: Published and verified: 32 ready-for-agent sub-issues and 43 native blocking relationships

tickets.title: Audit retained-data readiness for the scheduling MVP
tickets.delivers: A read-only readiness report identifying exactly which retained records need an approved repair policy before affected schema changes or monthly enforcement can proceed.
criteria: Inspect the actual records that must be retained, using read-only access, and report counts/categories of missing or ambiguous user statuses, missing event/template end times, missing current-owner assignment timestamps, and any unexpected user-certification verification data. Do not expose personal data in the report.
Document the agreed legacy active-slot to confirmed and deleted-slot to soft-deleted mappings, preserving identity, roles, explicit statuses, users, and relationships.
Distinguish slot creation from the current owner's assignment time; do not infer priority from UUIDs, a shared migration timestamp, or another unapproved fallback.

Produce an actionable migration-readiness result, including the specific product-owner decisions needed if incomplete retained data exists. Inspection is complete when these findings are recorded; approval of any repair policy remains an explicit prerequisite for the affected downstream migration.
Audit physical-delete operations and cascading declarations so the relevant workflow tickets can replace them without silently losing domain records.

Do not mutate records, run production migrations, or deploy. If live read access is unavailable, report that limitation rather than claiming the retained-data prerequisite is resolved; unrelated implementation can proceed.

tickets.title: Enforce hierarchical roles and independent Officer capabilities
tickets.delivers: Administrators can grant the two Officer capabilities in the UI, while existing application and authentication operations enforce the approved authority boundaries on the server.
criteria: Persist and manage exactly the scheduling-management and user-management Officer grants; ordinary Users cannot receive them, Officers cannot delegate them, and Administrator/Developer effectively have both.
Keep exactly one hierarchical role per user. Administrators can change User/Officer/Administrator roles; only Developers can grant Developer or change an existing Developer's role.

Resolve actor identity from the trusted session and protect existing calendar, profile, certification, authorization, onboarding, and relevant Better Auth/plugin operations. Client actor IDs, roles, grants, or completion flags cannot establish authority.

Preserve every Officer's full-profile viewing and saved-location-management authority independently of mutation grants. Restrict restoration to Developers and avoid a granular authorization-rules editor.
First consolidate only the guards/entry points necessary to close existing bypasses; retain the application stack and existing usable UI rather than introducing a separate architecture rewrite.

Introduce the minimal isolated PostgreSQL/session test harness with this behavior slice. Direct-operation and auth/plugin tests prove the role/grant matrix and bypass denials; UI checks verify grant controls reflect effective authority. Preserve explicit existing roles rather than inventing missing user lifecycle values.

tickets.title: Deliver authorized profile management and user type labels
tickets.delivers: Every Officer can view full profiles, and user managers can edit managed profile information and reusable user type labels through working profile screens.
criteria: Replace placeholder profile views with full permitted profile/contact information; every Officer can view others, while ordinary Users cannot query others' full profiles even through direct operations.
User managers can edit permitted managed profile fields and create/rename/assign reusable user type labels; viewing a profile never implicitly grants mutation authority.
Treat user type as a display label only, separate from system role, Officer grants, and scheduling eligibility.
Retain user type records through soft deletion and reject deletion while assigned to a non-deleted profile; deleted references alone do not block it.
Use current profile/type values in permitted responses and avoid adding historical snapshots or exposing extra profile fields through selection/combobox queries.

Verify direct-operation access and mutation denials for each audience, along with profile rendering and user type management. Later certification and history slices extend these views with their own domain information.

tickets.title: Activate verified registration through required onboarding
tickets.delivers: Email/password and Google users follow organization registration mode, verify their email, and complete required onboarding before ordinary scheduling access becomes active.
criteria: Persist organization registration mode with invitation-only as its initial value. Administrator/Developer can change it in the UI; open registration activates ordinary users after verified email and completed onboarding without approval.

Both authentication providers deny uninvited account creation in invitation-only mode and show the instruction to contact the organization. The invitation slice later supplies the permitted invited-identity path.

Require first name, last name, email, and a phone number with country code; accept ordinary formatting and normalize phone without phone verification. Middle name, image, and post-nominals remain optional; generate display name from name components.

Derive onboarding completion and activation server-side, preserve existing verified identity, and deny volunteer scheduling access to unverified, incomplete, invited, or inactive identities as appropriate. Do not trust a client-set completion timestamp.

Use controlled external Google/email adapters for auth-handler tests while exercising real application identity/session/database behavior. Verify both-provider gating and completed/incomplete onboarding outcomes through the UI and server.

Use the retained-data audit findings before changing required status/name fields. If retained data needs repair, obtain the explicit policy before that migration/activation behavior is enabled; do not invent statuses or change explicit existing roles. No production migration or deployment is authorized.

tickets.title: Create invited profiles and atomically claim their identities
tickets.delivers: A user manager can pre-create a profile, send/resend/revoke an invitation, and the volunteer can claim that same profile through either supported authentication method.
criteria: Provide a create-profile form with first/last name and email, optional middle name, and optional separate invitation sending; phone may be supplied at onboarding. Preserve the created profile when an invitation is revoked.
Deliver an invitation through the required email mechanism. Invitations do not expire; resend invalidates the previous link and revoke prevents claiming through that credential.

Verified case-insensitive matching email through email/password or Google claims the existing profile rather than creating a duplicate; preserve its identity and existing assignments. Review account linking against this verified identity contract.
Make claim/resend/revoke atomic: the first completed operation governs subsequent valid actions. A claimed profile cannot subsequently be treated as an unclaimed invitation.

In open mode, verified matching self-registration may claim an existing profile after invitation revocation, but revoked credentials remain unusable. Outstanding invitations survive a change to open mode.

Unclaimed profiles cannot obtain volunteer scheduling access until verified sign-in and required onboarding. Expose invited profiles as permitted scheduler assignment targets without making inactive users assignable.

Test both providers, mismatched/unverified identity, case-insensitive duplicates, stale invitation links, retained assignments, and claim/resend/revoke races with a test email sink and isolated database.

tickets.title: Create and invite profiles with per-row bulk results
tickets.delivers: User managers can submit a multi-row creation/invitation form and retain successful rows even when other rows fail.
criteria: Provide a multi-row form using the same profile creation and optional invitation commands as individual creation; do not add CSV upload.
Persist valid rows and report each invalid/duplicate row individually, including duplicate emails within the batch and emails belonging to existing profiles.
An existing-email row fails rather than silently editing, merging, or reinviting an existing profile.
Retain successful profile/invitation results when another row fails, and show which rows can be corrected without re-running successful creation implicitly.
Verify partial success, concurrent duplicate creation, per-row authorization/validation, delivery outcomes, and useful row feedback through operation-level and focused form tests.

tickets.title: Edit own profiles and safely verify email changes
tickets.delivers: Users can maintain their basic profile and change email without making the unverified new address a sign-in identifier prematurely.
criteria: Expose own basic profile editing with required name/contact validation, normalized country-code phone, generated display name, and optional middle name/photo/post-nominals.
Do not allow own profile editing to change role, Officer grants, user type, verification state, lifecycle status, or onboarding authority.
Store/request the pending email change without replacing the currently verified sign-in identity until the new address is verified; the existing verified sign-in remains usable in the interim.
Send verification at the new address and a security notice at the old address through the authentication email mechanism, without an operational in-app email-change notification.

Verify successful and unverified changes, conflicting identities, spoofed ownership, both supported authentication paths where relevant, and correct destination addresses using controlled email/provider adapters.

tickets.title: Manage the hierarchical certification catalog
tickets.delivers: User managers can create, organize, rename, and safely remove reusable certification definitions in the catalog UI.
criteria: Support the existing parent/child certification hierarchy through working user-manager screens and server validation; training levels and specialties use this same catalog.
Renaming preserves certification identity and changes displayed names wherever that certification is referenced.
Reject invalid hierarchy relationships, including cycles, without creating another eligibility dimension or certification effective/expiration dates.

Soft-delete catalog records, exclude them from normal selection, and block deletion for current non-deleted children or other existing live references. Later relation/expression slices add their reference guards with the new references.
Test authorized and unauthorized catalog changes, hierarchy behavior, stable identity on rename, and retained deleted references through server operations and focused catalog UI checks.

tickets.title: Submit and review certifications with a shared inbox
tickets.delivers: Volunteers submit certifications, user managers review them, and a usable in-app inbox supports shared review state, personal dismissal, and rejection messages.
criteria: Persist a user-certification relation with pending/verified/rejected status separate from the catalog. Volunteer submission is pending; manager creation/approval is verified immediately.
Allow own pending edit while keeping pending, own pending withdrawal by soft deletion, and rejected edit/resubmission on the same record. Only a user manager can remove verified certifications.

Provide the shared user-management review queue, visible to effective user managers, without claiming work. Each recipient has independent read/dismiss state; resolving the underlying submission closes the item globally.

Pending edits keep the same review item current; withdrawal resolves it. Rejection retains the record and delivers an optional reviewer comment to the volunteer. Approval does not create a certification-approval notification.

Introduce the reusable in-app personal/shared notification behavior through this working flow. Delivered text is copied independently of later comment/review changes; notification/comment records use appropriate soft deletion.
Display certification information on permitted profiles and block catalog deletion while linked by non-deleted user-certification records; deleted links alone do not block.

Test full submit/edit/withdraw/approve/reject/resubmit flows, mutation authority versus full-profile viewing, individual versus global state, immutable delivered text, and intentional absence of approval messages.

tickets.title: Author position eligibility with branch-preserving explanations
tickets.delivers: Schedulers can author validated nested position requirements and users can understand the alternative qualification branches.
criteria: Extend position management with arbitrary nested AND/OR over verified exact/descendant-inclusive certifications and hierarchical minimum system role.
Validate expression shape and referenced records on the server. Reject NOT, exact-role predicates, user-type predicates, and other unapproved dimensions.

No expression permits otherwise assignable active users, retaining the scheduler exception for invited profiles. Unverified certifications and user type do not satisfy eligibility or change platform authority.

Use a shared eligibility behavior for subsequent assignment/replacement/recheck commands; provide a working requirement/explanation UI that preserves OR alternatives rather than treating every leaf as mandatory.
Keep expressions global to positions, without event/template alternatives. Editing alone does not scan current assignments or preview conflicts.
Block certification deletion for non-deleted expression references and keep historical references renderable.
Test nested alternatives, exact versus descendant matching, role inheritance, empty requirements, invalid references/language, and explanation rendering at the approved operation/UI seams.

tickets.title: Publish valid events and privacy-safe public listings
tickets.delivers: Schedulers create/edit events with valid local times, and signed-out visitors see only permitted current event details until event end.
criteria: Require event start and end with end strictly later on the same America/New_York calendar date; new events publish immediately without drafts or cross-midnight support.
Implement authoritative upcoming/in-progress/past boundaries: upcoming before start, in progress from start inclusive to end exclusive, past at end.

Provide signed-out event listing/detail responses containing only title/name, date, time, location, description. Do not return staffing, positions, capacity, vacancy counts, assignments, roster names, or profile data.
Remove cancelled/deleted events and remove public events exactly at end; no public past-event access. Use explicit audience projections, not browser-only hiding.

Schedulers can edit past events indefinitely and use current related data without snapshots, closure deadlines, or attendance outcomes. Assignment notifications are added when the assignment/cancellation slice integrates them.
Apply the retained-data audit findings before enforcing required end times; missing existing end values need explicit correction rather than an inferred duration.
Verify direct public payloads and routes, timezone/host independence, positive duration and local-date boundaries, past editing, and exact start/end behavior with a controllable clock.

tickets.title: Manage saved locations and copy their values into event forms
tickets.delivers: Every Officer can maintain saved locations and use editable autofill in event forms without later source edits changing existing events.
criteria: Provide saved-location creation/editing/soft deletion for every Officer, Administrator, and Developer independently of scheduling/user-management grants.
Event forms allow manual name/address entry or saved-location autofill that copies values into editable event data.
Later saved-location edits/deletion do not propagate into existing event values. Keep saved-location management authority distinct from permission to save an event.
Retain deleted saved locations for later Developer recovery and exclude them from normal selection.

Verify full Officer access matrix, unauthorized ordinary-user attempts, editable copied values, and no propagation through operation-level and focused form tests. Template autofill is integrated when its complete template slice lands.

tickets.title: Assign volunteers through lifecycle-aware shifts and atomic capacity
tickets.delivers: Schedulers can create shifts and assign active or invited users with authoritative confirmed/pending state, reserved capacity, conflict explanations, and in-app outcomes.
criteria: Introduce the approved confirmed/pending/available/rejected/cancelled slot lifecycle, orthogonal soft deletion, assignment-creation timestamp, and latest transition comment/actor/time. Confirmed/pending/available occupy capacity; rejected/cancelled/deleted do not.
Provide one live shift per event/position, positive integer capacity, and UI/server rejection of capacity reductions below active-capacity occupancy.

Before changing the mutation behavior, consolidate existing assignment/capacity writes into one authoritative command and select a supported transactional/concurrency mechanism compatible with the application database adapter. Keep the existing stack.

Scheduler assignment admits active and invited profiles, rejects inactive users, evaluates the current eligibility/duplicate-event conflicts, and offers suppress-all confirmed or unsuppressed pending when conflicts exist. No conflict lists or suppression history are persisted.
Atomically create the assignment and grow maximum slots by one on scheduler overflow. Concurrent writes cannot produce inconsistent occupancy or lose an update.

Connect pending assignments to the shared scheduling queue and deliver the approved affected-volunteer assignment messages through the existing inbox. Optional comments never become backend-required, and absent new comment clears prior text.

Preserve legacy records with agreed active/deleted mappings. If retained assignments lack current-owner timestamps, require the explicitly approved repair policy before dependent behavior is enabled; never invent monthly priority.

Verify direct authorization, active/invited/inactive assignment, confirmed/pending occupancy, duplicate live shifts, capacity races and overflow rollback, retained data, and current-state UI. Monthly-limit evaluation extends this command in its own slice before volunteer signup is enabled.

tickets.title: Show volunteer rosters and restricted assignment history
tickets.delivers: Active volunteers can browse events and rosters and access their own relevant history without receiving other volunteers' review/profile information.
criteria: Show active signed-in volunteers upcoming events regardless of certifications, roster names, and their own pending status. Later available-slot actions use the same restricted projection.
Omit other volunteers' pending/review/conflict indicators and staff decision comments from volunteer responses; roster access never grants full profile access.
At event end, permit volunteer past-event access only where that volunteer was assigned, including retained cancelled-event relationships. Unrelated history and direct query bypasses are denied.
Schedulers can access all scheduling events/history, including cancellations and review information; public responses remain limited to the public projection.
Render current related profile/position/user-type data, keeping permitted past-event joins renderable after catalog soft deletion without snapshots or event closure.
Verify exact start/end boundaries and adversarial direct responses for public, volunteer, Officer without scheduling grant, and scheduler audiences; add focused roster/history UI checks.

tickets.title: Enforce monthly event participation and assignment priority
tickets.delivers: Schedulers configure the monthly limit and assignment decisions consistently rank distinct event participation in America/New_York.
criteria: Persist the organization-wide monthly limit, default 3, with scheduler-only settings UI/server changes.

Count distinct non-cancelled/non-deleted events with remaining confirmed/pending/available participation, including past events in the event-start month; exclude rejected/cancelled/deleted assignments and avoid candidate double-counting.

Rank each event by the earliest timestamp among the volunteer's remaining active-capacity assignments in that event, not confirmation time. Multiple positions count once; removing the earliest may change priority.

Evaluate in America/New_York event-start month regardless of request/replacement time or host timezone. Preserve same-event priority and support new timestamps for different-event moves/replacement integration.

Integrate over-limit conflicts into scheduler assignment explanations and suppression/pending decisions. Only participation beyond the first N is over-limit; overlapping separate-event times are not a conflict rule.
Changing a limit does not perform opt-out detection scans/previews. Subsequent resolution/recheck slices add their respective targeted behaviors without conflating them.
Refuse to enable enforcement over incomplete retained assignment timestamps without the approved policy from the conditional audit prerequisite.

Verify first-N ordering, pending reservations, multiple positions, past current-month events, candidate exclusion, concurrent same-user requests, year/month/DST boundaries, and settings authorization through real-database operations.

tickets.title: Review pending slots and suppress current conflicts
tickets.delivers: Schedulers can approve or reject reserved pending assignments in the shared review UI and volunteers receive the appropriate immutable decision message.
criteria: Provide shared pending-assignment review without claiming items; access follows effective scheduling capability, not full-profile viewing or user-management capability.
Approve into confirmed or reject into retained rejected state with optional comment. Rejection frees occupancy and monthly participation; permit later same-shift retry as a new slot.
Approval/suppression covers all current conflicts as one decision and never changes a position expression or persists conflict/suppression identifiers/history.
Keep only latest transition metadata; a new transition without comment clears prior text, while already delivered decision text remains unchanged.
Resolve underlying review globally while keeping personal read/dismiss independent, and send the approved volunteer approval/rejection notifications.
Make pending assignments read-only for end users, showing generic contact-schedulers instructions rather than editing/withdrawal or a new in-app contact workflow.
Verify decision authorization, concurrent/stale reviews, released capacity/monthly participation, retry, comment optionality/clearing, immutable messages, and shared-versus-personal queue behavior.

tickets.title: Request vacant seats with confirmed or pending outcomes
tickets.delivers: An active volunteer can request a vacant seat before event start, receive one confirmation when eligible, or reserve a pending seat with understandable conflict reasons.
criteria: Allow only active, verified, onboarded volunteers to request strictly before event start through the authoritative assignment command.
Passing current eligibility/monthly checks creates confirmed; failed eligibility/monthly checks explain reasons preserving alternative branches and permit explicit pending submission.
Pending reserves the seat and monthly participation, displays own pending status, creates the shared scheduling review item, and is never a waitlist.
Hard-block another active-capacity assignment in the same event and full shifts without an available replacement. Do not reserve an over-capacity pending request.
Send exactly one confirmed-self-signup in-app confirmation; pending shows status/review without a duplicate confirmation. Reject end-user slot changes at start and any pending edit/withdrawal.
Retained rejection does not block a new same-shift request. End users cannot atomically switch positions.

Test successful/pending/fourth-distinct-event outcomes, full/duplicate blocking, two concurrent last-seat requests, simultaneous same-user requests, exact start cutoff, retry, and branch-preserving signup UI.

tickets.title: Move and remove assignments through scheduler drag and drop
tickets.delivers: Schedulers can reassign or remove volunteers atomically, including after start, with correct capacity, priority, and notifications.
criteria: Provide scheduler drag/drop reassignment through the same authoritative command rather than an alternate unchecked mutation path.
Move atomically with current eligibility/monthly/duplicate-event checks, optional suppress-all or pending decision, and destination capacity expansion when required.
Preserve assignment timestamp for a position move within one event; start a new timestamp for a move to another event and correctly recalculate remaining earliest participation priority.
Remove an assignment by soft deletion, release its capacity/monthly participation, retain original data, and deliver approved affected-volunteer messages with optional comments.
Permit scheduler action on in-progress/past events indefinitely while preserving end-user restrictions.
Prevent stale drag/drop/reassignment from overwriting a newer owner/state. Failed moves leave source/destination/notifications consistent without partial changes.
Verify real-database races, timestamp/priority behavior, overflow rollback, inactive target rejection, optional comments, notifications, and focused drag/drop UI behavior.

tickets.title: Automatically confirm affected eligible pending assignments
tickets.delivers: Existing pending assignments confirm automatically when their blockers disappear, without demoting confirmed assignments or introducing edit-driven conflict scans.
criteria: Reconsider only affected upcoming pending slots when certification approval, qualifying role change, reduced participation, relaxed requirements, or increased limit removes blockers.

Wire the existing qualification/role/position/limit/removal/move operations to targeted resolution; later release/replacement/cancellation commands must invoke the same behavior for affected participation.
Confirm only when all checks pass and the event ranks within the first N distinct participations, including past participation in that month and pending priority.

With A/B/C/D creation order and limit 3, approving B's needed certification can confirm B while D stays pending. Scheduler-approved over-limit confirmed events do not displace earlier pending priority.
Never demote confirmed, scan globally for new conflicts, require opt-in for resolution, or resolve withdrawal requests. Slots at/after start stay untouched.
Generate explanatory latest system comment and one in-app confirmation on successful automatic confirmation, resolving the shared review item globally without rewriting old messages.

Verify scoped effects and intentional non-effects across all existing triggers using real-database operations and a controllable clock, including no detection preview or volunteer demotion notification.

tickets.title: Withdraw confirmed assignments and review late requests
tickets.delivers: Volunteers withdraw immediately outside the late window or retain responsibility in available state inside it, with scheduler release/denial controls.
criteria: Persist and expose scheduler control of the organization-wide late-withdrawal window, default 72 hours, using event start and the operation clock.
Strictly before start, a confirmed volunteer outside the window immediately soft-deletes the slot with on-screen success and no additional in-app notification.
Inside the window set available, retaining incumbent responsibility, occupied capacity, monthly participation, and a shared withdrawal review item.
Display available status and incumbent name in the permitted roster projection. Available is replacement availability, not an understaffed vacancy or pending candidate.
Scheduler release soft-deletes and makes a genuinely vacant seat without a volunteer notification solely for release approval; denial returns confirmed and notifies with optional comment.

Release resolves the underlying withdrawal/warning and invokes targeted resolution for affected pending participation. End users cannot change pending slots or make any slot change at/after start; schedulers can act indefinitely, and available can persist after start.
Verify both sides of the configured window, exact start cutoff, preserved owner/capacity/monthly rank, generic pending contact UI, denial/release message rules, and affected automatic resolution.

tickets.title: Claim available slots with atomic volunteer replacement
tickets.delivers: A qualifying volunteer or authorized scheduler can replace an incumbent in the same available slot without extra capacity or a pending replacement candidate.
criteria: Provide an available-slot claim action strictly before start for active end users; require all eligibility, monthly, and duplicate-event checks to pass or hard-block.
Permit scheduler replacement after start/past end, but require immediate suppress-all for conflicts; never leave a replacement pending.

Atomically update the existing slot to the replacement owner and confirmed state, preserving slot identity/capacity while assigning the replacement a new assignment timestamp and latest replacement comment.

Release the incumbent's event participation only if no other active-capacity assignment remains there; use the event-start month for both users and trigger targeted resolution for the released participation.

Resolve withdrawal/review warnings, notify the released incumbent, and use the ordinary confirmation path for exactly one replacement confirmation; do not create a second candidate/incumbent slot or history archive.
Concurrent claims have one winner, stale ownership changes do not overwrite a newer replacement, and failure leaves the incumbent and occupancy intact.

Verify same-slot identity, January-event/December-claim counting, new priority, failed checks, scheduler suppression, concurrency, message deduplication, and takeable-slot UI. Once a release makes it vacant, ordinary pending signup rules apply.

tickets.title: Request scoped conflict rechecks without implicit scans
tickets.delivers: Staff editors can explicitly recheck the relevant upcoming assignments, while ordinary edits/reads remain free of conflict scans and available incumbents retain replacement availability.
criteria: Add default-OFF scoped opt-in controls to user role/certification, position requirement, event date/time, and monthly-limit edits; schedulers can explicitly request all upcoming slots.

Use the approved scopes: that user, that position, the changed event if its new start is upcoming, and affected event-start months. User-management-only Officers may request the edited user's check without manual slot authority.
Without explicit detection request, do not scan assignments, show conflict preview/count, or generate scan messages; preserve separate targeted automatic resolution when blockers disappear.

Exclude slots once start is reached. Current conflicts demote confirmed to pending even after previous suppression; failing pending remains pending. Generate explanatory system comment and scheduler review/own pending state without volunteer notification.

Available with conflicts remains available and gets a generic scheduler-only review item with requester/time, without persisted conflict details. Viewing does not scan; an explicit recheck supplies current reasons.

Suppression clears the warning until another requested check; release/replacement resolves it and unresolved warnings remain actionable after start. Integrate with replacement if present, and require later replacement code to preserve this resolution contract.

Verify every scope, grants, repeated/suppressed conflicts, no-scan reads/edits, immutable delivered messages, available warning lifecycle, and no automatic start/closure cleanup through server and focused controls tests.

tickets.title: Notify event changes and irreversibly cancel staffed events
tickets.delivers: Assigned volunteers receive logistical event changes, and schedulers can irreversibly cancel an event while retaining the appropriate notification/history access.
criteria: Notify assigned volunteers on date/time/location changes and cancellation; title/description edits do not notify. Requested rechecks remain independently default-OFF rather than implicit scans.
Expose scheduler cancellation with standard message plus optional custom text; atomically change all non-deleted active-capacity assignments to cancelled and retain their data.
Cancellation releases capacity/monthly participation, resolves underlying assignment/withdrawal review work, and runs targeted pending resolution only for affected released participation.
Cancellation cannot be undone. Public/ordinary volunteer calendars hide it, affected volunteers retain notification/history access, and schedulers retain full scheduling/history access.
Keep cancelled/rejected/already-deleted assignments out of newly cancelled active recipients and avoid duplicate notification delivery or partial state under concurrent cancellation/assignment.
Verify event-change delivery/non-delivery, immutable messages, cancellation atomicity, current participant recipient selection, released monthly priority, and direct history/calendar projections.

tickets.title: Soft-delete shifts and events with cascade provenance
tickets.delivers: Schedulers can remove staffing or eligible events without physical deletion, while provenance distinguishes descendants removed together from those deleted independently.
criteria: Removing a shift represents zero capacity, soft-deletes its active slots, releases participation, and notifies active-slot volunteers with optional custom text.
Block event deletion while active-capacity assignments exist; cancelled/rejected/deleted slots do not block. Cancellation or explicit removals can make the event deletable.
Permitted event deletion atomically soft-deletes its shifts and slots, preserving records, timestamps, and required links. Remove physical-delete/cascade-loss paths in these workflows.
Track root deletion operation provenance so independently deleted descendants retain their own deletion identity and are distinguishable for later recovery.
Resolve affected underlying review items and invoke targeted pending resolution for released participation. Domain records and delivered notifications are retained appropriately.

Verify deletion restrictions, entire-shift recipients, atomic rollback, normal-view filtering, independent-descendant provenance, and historical referential rendering. Later threshold creation must integrate its owned records into these cascade rules.

tickets.title: Configure and reconcile timed understaffing alerts
tickets.delivers: Schedulers configure optional per-shift thresholds and see real time-driven Warning/Critical alerts without relying on page visits or unrelated edits.
criteria: Provide zero-or-more event-shift thresholds with lead time in days/hours and fixed Warning/amber or Critical/red; no separate minimum-filled target or custom severity colors.
Count confirmed/pending/available as filled against the shift's full maximum. An incumbent's available slot alone does not cause understaffing.

Choose and implement a supported server reconciliation mechanism that runs without page visits or unrelated changes; expose one current highest-unresolved-severity alert per shift with lower thresholds in details.

Resolve alerts on filled capacity, cancellation/deletion, or required event end, including time-driven expiry. Use shared scheduler notification/recipient semantics and integrate threshold records with shift/event soft deletion.
Persist domain/notification state rather than rendering client-only urgency. Keep assignment rechecks separate; alert reconciliation does not scan for assignment conflicts.

Verify threshold activation/end using the reconciliation entry point, controlled clock and isolated database, occupancy for every slot state, fixed presentation, repeated evaluation without duplicate actionable items, and no interaction needed.

tickets.title: Resolve thresholds individually and reopen recurring understaffing
tickets.delivers: Schedulers can manually resolve the current threshold without silencing later urgency, and alerts return when a filled shift becomes vacant again.
criteria: Expose manual threshold-specific global resolution even while vacancies remain; reaching a different/new threshold creates an actionable alert according to severity/lead-time rules.
Filling a shift resolves the applicable alert; a later vacancy while a threshold remains active makes the alert actionable again.
Recompute one highest unresolved severity per shift and keep lower thresholds in details without making resolution shift-wide or event-wide.
Personal dismiss/read affects only that recipient and never globally resolves or suppresses new urgency.

Verify manual resolution, later threshold activation, fill/vacate cycles, multiple scheduler recipients, repeat reconciliation, and cancellation/deletion/end termination with controlled time and focused alert controls.

tickets.title: Create events from independent templates with copied alerts
tickets.delivers: Schedulers maintain templates and create one event on a selected date with copied details, local times, location, positions/capacities, and alert thresholds.
criteria: Provide template create/edit and one-date event creation, validating required same-date positive-duration local times and at most one live position association per template.

Copy event details, time values interpreted on the selected America/New_York date, manual/autofilled location values, capacities, and all configured thresholds atomically into independent event records.
Saved-location autofill copies editable values; later saved-location edits do not change templates/events. Later template edits do not propagate to created events.
No threshold is required, and templates have no eligibility alternatives, recurring generation, or live alert linkage. Any source-template identifier is optional provenance only.
Template soft deletion is not blocked by events created from it; preserve created event data and rendering. Record provenance needed for restoring deleted template-owned records later.
Require explicit correction of retained missing template end times under the audit prerequisite rather than inferring them.

Verify complete copied values, independence after edits/deletion, duplicate-position and duration validation, atomic creation rollback, timezone boundaries, saved-location form behavior, and copied threshold reconciliation.

tickets.title: Complete reference-data deletion safeguards and retained history
tickets.delivers: Staff can safely remove positions, certifications, user types, templates, and saved locations using the approved live-reference restrictions rather than physical deletion or blanket historical blocks.
criteria: Apply final reference checks across the now-working catalog, position, user type, template, and location management UIs/server operations, retaining appropriate deletion metadata and owned-record provenance.
Block position deletion while referenced by future events or templates, but permit it when only past-event references remain; past views must still render retained position data.

Block certification deletion for non-deleted user links, child certifications, or expression references. Block user type deletion while assigned to a non-deleted profile; deleted links alone do not block either.
Events created from a template never block that template's deletion. Saved-location copies remain independent and deleted records disappear from normal selectors.
Avoid physical domain deletion or blanket rejection merely because historical foreign keys exist. Audit remaining catalog/template/location physical-delete paths.
Verify each restriction with live versus deleted references, past/current joins, user-type label neutrality, copied-value independence, and direct mutation authority.

tickets.title: Deactivate users with immediate session revocation
tickets.delivers: User managers can deactivate a user only after upcoming active responsibilities are removed, and successful deactivation immediately ends access.
criteria: Expose authorized activation/deactivation controls on managed profiles, preserving identity, role, explicit lifecycle data, and relationships.
Block deactivation for any upcoming non-deleted confirmed/pending/available assignment; exclude cancelled/rejected/deleted assignments and use start-strictly-future semantics.

Successful deactivation revokes existing sessions immediately, prevents new sign-in through both providers, and prevents assignment from every server path. Invited-profile assignment remains the approved exception rather than allowing inactive assignment.
Keep domain profiles retained. Removing revoked/expired sessions and one-use verification/reset tokens is allowed and must not preserve usable revoked credentials.
Avoid a race in which deactivation and assignment both succeed leaving an inactive user newly assigned; verify using concurrent real-database operations.
Test successful/blocked deactivation, active-session invalidation, exact upcoming boundary, both auth paths, invited/inactive differences, and profile UI feedback.

tickets.title: Restore profiles and reference records through Developer recovery
tickets.delivers: Developers can inspect and recover retained profiles, reference data, templates, and notification records while preserving original data and revoked-credential safety.
criteria: Provide a Developer-only recovery surface and server commands for retained user profiles, user types, certification catalog/user-certification records, positions, saved locations, templates/owned records, and soft-deleted notification/comment records where applicable. Include Developer soft deletion of historical items subject to their existing domain restrictions; no domain physical deletion.
Preserve original business values, statuses, timestamps, and identity. Restore only owned descendants deleted with the root operation; never revive independently deleted records implicitly.

Validate current reference/hierarchy/uniqueness integrity atomically before recovery, including restoration of links to currently deleted parents. Do not silently change approved eligibility or user-type semantics to make restoration pass.
Keep lifecycle deactivation and domain deletion distinct; profile recovery must not revive expired/revoked authentication credentials or invent a new active status.

Recovery is quiet: no new volunteer/staff/review messages, assignment rechecks, automatic pending confirmations, or redelivery of existing notifications. Existing review state and delivered text remain unchanged.

Verify Developer-only direct access, preserved values and soft-deletion boundaries, structural rollback, deleted-reference link checks, notification/comment retention without a full transition archive, and quiet qualification/profile recovery.

tickets.title: Quietly restore slots and shifts without workflow replay
tickets.delivers: Developers can restore a standalone slot or shift with original assignment state/priority while recoverable scheduling conflicts are suppressed and structural failures reject atomically.
criteria: Extend Developer recovery to standalone slots and shifts, preserving original owner, business values, assignment timestamps, and confirmed/pending/available states and latest metadata.

Suppress monthly-limit, eligibility, and duplicate-event conflicts as the approved exceptional restoration decision; do not persist conflict lists/suppression history or turn restoration into a new signup.

Reject duplicate live event/position associations, insufficient capacity, inactive users, and active assignments beneath cancelled or still-deleted parents. Restore a shift and only its cascade-deleted children atomically.
Create no new volunteer/staff/review notifications, rechecks, automatic confirmations, or message redelivery; preserve existing review states and keep confirmed confirmed and pending pending.

Restored participation retains original monthly priority. Do not automatically demote/flag/notify another newly over-limit assignment; later ordinary evaluations and explicit rechecks include restored data.

Restore owned alert configuration only according to cascade provenance and allow ordinary scheduled understaffing evaluation to resume, without conflating that later evaluation with restoration workflow replay.

Verify suppressed versus structural failures, whole-operation rollback, independently deleted descendants, states/timestamps, no automatic side effects, later explicit rechecks/signup evaluation, and subsequent normal alert reconciliation.

tickets.title: Restore event cascades atomically and preserve cancellation
tickets.delivers: Developers can recover an event and exactly the descendants deleted with it in one quiet operation, without reinstating a cancelled event or partially restoring invalid staffing.
criteria: Provide event recovery through the Developer surface and the established quiet restoration command boundary, restoring the original event and only descendants sharing its root deletion provenance.
Keep independently deleted shifts, slots, and owned records deleted; retain business values, original timestamps, assignment states, and copied configuration.
Validate all event/shift/slot structural conditions before commit and roll back the entire event on any failure; never partially recover the event.
Preserve a cancelled event's cancellation and cancelled slot states. Reject any active assignment beneath a cancelled or still-deleted parent rather than using recovery to reinstate it.
Suppress only the approved recoverable scheduling conflicts, retaining original monthly priority without notifying/demoting other assignments.

Create no action-triggered volunteer/staff/review messages, assignment rechecks, automatic confirmations, or old-message redelivery. Existing review state remains intact; ordinary later alert evaluation and explicit checks continue normally.

Verify a complete delete/recover workflow, independent prior deletions, all-or-nothing structural failures, cancelled-event recovery, visibility through normal permitted views, and quiet side effects through real-database operations.
